messages:
maria: Hey team — opening a request for eu-west3 account. We had a large training rollout this morning and several pods failed during startup when we scaled to ~50 GPUs. Symptoms look like ephemeral external IP / SNAT exhaustion and some forwarding-rule quota errors. Need help with: increase ephemeral external IP quota, increase forwarding-rule quota, and a Private Service Connect / peering path to shared-services to avoid egress NAT costs. Also asking for guidance on AZ-affinity for NAT to reduce cross-AZ egress costs.

kevin: Can you paste the pod/cluster logs? Is this Cloud NAT or per-node NAT? Also do we know if the workloads are using hostNetwork or hitting external endpoints a lot during init (model fetches, license checks)?

maria: Logs snippet below (truncated):
```
Error: failed to allocate external IP: quota exceeded (region: europe-west3)
Pod: train-abc-123 initContainer pull-data: connection reset
kubelet: SNAT port exhaustion, failed connections: 312/900
```
We use Cloud NAT on our shared egress setup plus transient external IPs for some control-plane traffic. Model pulls go to artifact-store in shared-services for now.

raj: Quick inventory: the project currently has 24 ephemeral external IP addresses and 50 forwarding rules in eu-west3. For 50 nodes doing heavy egress we should target ~110 ephemeral IPs and bump forwarding rules to 200. PSC (Private Service Connect) connections are currently 3; we need more PSC connectors to shared-services for high parallelism. I can start the quota requests but need business approval for the temporary cost delta.

sophie: Approved for a temporary increase up to 200 ephemeral IPs and 200 forwarding rules for 90 days, provided we implement PrivateLink/PSC and AZ affinity to reduce ongoing cost. Please keep the window as short as possible and add a rollback plan.

kevin: For AZ affinity approaches we have two options: 1) Cloud NAT with per-vm port allocation (increase min_ports_per_vm) so a single NAT can support more endpoints; 2) per-AZ NAT gateways (or per-AZ Cloud NAT configs) and schedule nodes with nodeAffinity/daemonset to ensure egress stays AZ-local. My quick terraform snippet:
```
resource "google_compute_router" "r" {
  name = "nat-router-eu3"
}
resource "google_compute_router_nat" "nat" {
  name = "nat-eu3"
  router = google_compute_router.r.name
  min_ports_per_vm = 2048
  source_subnetwork_ip_ranges_to_nat = "ALL_SUBNETWORKS_ALL_IP_RANGES"
}
```
If we go per-AZ, we should create NAT configs per subnetwork and use topology-aware routing + node labels so pods prefer local AZ. That reduces cross-AZ bandwidth and keeps SNAT ports per NAT small.

maria: Sounds good. Also would like to avoid long-lived public IPs where possible — PSC to shared-services (artifact store + model-registry) will help. Can someone open PSC quota (Private Service Connect endpoints) and VPC peering increases for redwood-eu3 -> shared-services? We often hit the 3 PSC connection limit.

infra-bot: Ticket created: GCP-Q-2026 — Request increases for project redwood-eu3: ephemeral external IPs -> 200, forwarding rules -> 200, PSC endpoints -> 50, peering routes -> 100. Assigned to: kevin. Priority: P2. Estimated SLA: 3-5 business days. Reference: https://console.cloud.google.com/quotas?project=redwood-eu3

raj: I'll add short-term Prom alerts for SNAT port utilization and failed external IP allocation. Suggest rule: alert if avg_snat_port_utilization > 0.85 for 5m. I'll post the rule in the monitoring repo.

maria: Thanks. We'll pause further large-scale training rollouts until quota confirmation or we flip to PSC path. Next steps: kevin to own quota tickets, raj to add alerts, infra-bot to update ticket status here, sophie to re-open cost window if needed.

kevin: On it. Also putting a quick runbook note: if we see this again, temporarily scale down node parallelism and stagger model pulls with randomized backoff to reduce burst egress.

maria: 👍 will update team and schedule a short post-mortem once we have ticket outcomes.
